contentHtml:
New Delhi: The screening records of cancer patients should be linked with their Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) IDs to ensure continuity of care across healthcare facilities, Union health ministry said on Saturday.Speaking at the National Cancer Grid (NCG) Annual Meeting 2026 here, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava stressed the need to leverage India's digital health infrastructure for interoperable health records, responsible data sharing and evidence-based cancer care.

She also launched 'NCG VISHWAS', an AI-enabled patient education initiative covering breast, cervical and oral cancers in Hindi, Marathi, Tamil and English, the Union ministry said in a statement.

Advt

'VISHWAS' -- Videos to Support Health, Wellness, Awareness and Self-care -- provides information on cancer prevention, diagnosis, treatment and long-term care and will be disseminated through the NCG network of hospitals and healthcare partners.

Srivastava said more than 153 crore cancer screenings have been conducted so far under national health programmes at 1.87 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs.These include 37.1 crore screenings for oral cancer, 17.4 crore for breast cancer and 9.7 crore for cervical cancer, she said."With around 99 crore ABHA IDs created and about 100 crore health records linked," the digital health infrastructure can help ensure continuity of care as patients move from primary to secondary and tertiary facilities, including hospitals empanelled under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), Srivastava said.

With patients' consent, health records should be accessible to healthcare providers at different levels of care, she said.Srivastava said NCG VISHWAS could be disseminated through ASHA and Anganwadi workers and community platforms to strengthen cancer awareness and help patients and families access reliable information.She also suggested making the videos available through platforms such as Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and Swasth Bharat portals.

Highlighting the importance of affordability in cancer care, Srivastava referred to initiatives such as trade margin rationalisation for cancer medicines and financial support under AB PM-JAY for vulnerable and marginalised patients.

Advt

Around Rs 27,000 crore has been provided towards cancer care under the scheme, she said.Srivastava also called for AIIMS institutions with oncology facilities to become part of the National Cancer Grid and encouraged member hospitals to collaborate with the Pan-AIIMS Research Consortium for cancer research.

She said data, with patients' consent, could be used to advance cancer care and research.The Union health secretary highlighted the continuum of cancer care under the National Health Mission, from screening at the primary level to diagnosis at district hospitals and treatment at medical colleges and AB PM-JAY empanelled hospitals.

Advt

She also flagged the provision of day care cancer centres at district hospitals, technology-enabled radiology services to address workforce shortages and strengthening of oncology facilities at the 22 new AIIMS.Calling screening critical for early detection, Srivastava urged stakeholders to work together to strengthen cancer screening and ensure affordable healthcare.Dr C S Pramesh, Convener, National Cancer Grid, said NCG VISHWAS combines the grid's clinical expertise with technology and artificial intelligence (AI) to make reliable, clinician-reviewed information available to patients and families in various languages.

The NCG Annual Meeting 2026 is being held over two days in Mumbai and brings together more than 300 cancer-centre leaders, policymakers, global cancer control organisations, patient groups, technology developers and industry leaders.The National Cancer Grid comprises more than 400 cancer centres, research institutions and patient groups working towards improving cancer care through standardised protocols, quality assurance, capacity building and collaborative research.
